name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in enforce mode on a forked repo for one week. This gives us real-world data on how it handles code changes without risking the main project. The trade-off is the extra effort to set up and monitor the fork, but we gain actionable insights into its safety and effectiveness.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just the fork’s maintenance overhead—it’s that PR-Agent’s dry-run mode normalizes noisy, low-value feedback as "safe." A better alternative is testing it on a low-stakes branch in the main repo first, where we can measure actual impact without fragmenting our workflow. Settle it by running a 24-hour pilot on a non-critical PR and comparing the signal-to-noise ratio before committing to a fork.
